rubric_items.reason: Each acceptance criterion (L16-L22) maps to REQ-1..REQ-9. The follow-up goal in the user story and any rates are listed under Out of scope with a reason.
Criterion 2 is split into separate Completed and No-show counts, and criterion 5 into list, history and rest of page. Each REQ describes one behaviour that a tester can check.

Every known REQ cites the ticket or answer A-01. The label wording is a default the author picked, but it sits under Out of scope instead of Assumed. REQ-6 also cites user-story lines that say nothing about a time window.
The ticket does not clash with the baseline. The time-window gap against the glossary Period was asked as Q-01, and the user answered it.
Only one question was asked. It is real, it offered three concrete options, it had a proposed default, and it is answered and recorded.
The wording is plain. Completed, No-show, Scheduled and Cancelled match the glossary. The terms missing from the glossary are named and traced to ticket lines.

findings.text: REQ-6 (counting window) cites ticket L12-L13. Those lines are the user story and say nothing about a time window or a period picker. Only answer A-01 supports REQ-6.
